name: sherlock_looks_into_it
title: Sherlock looks into how others do a new kind of work and its suggestions land on the page

steps.say: I want help picking car wash sites to open
steps.reply: I've got two prior car‑wash efforts in your world — an open **Austin gates‑first screener** (zoning/traffic/competitor gates, already built and passing) and a **Scorecard with an investor memo** that you removed this morning. I've put three quick questions on a card (market, who the output is for, and whether to resume or restart) so I build the right thing instead of guessing or redoing work you already tossed.

steps.say: It's for me, to decide which sites to pursue and brief my investors. Sites come from brokers by email. Today I check households within 3 miles and the traffic on the road, then score visibility and access from 1 to 10 with a note each, and write a memo to investors. Thresholds: 45,000 households, 30,000 cars a day. Start with Austin. Go ahead and write it up.
steps.reply:
I've drafted the page. Here's the gist:

- **Intake**: Alpha watches Gmail for broker emails with a site and adds it as a candidate — I didn't find any car-wash broker emails there yet, so I flagged that as an assumption to check.
- **Gates**: Alpha looks up households within 3 miles (Census) and traffic on the road (TxDOT/Travis County GIS), marking Pass/Fail against your 45,000 / 30,000 thresholds.
- **Scoring**: visibility and access stay yours, 1–10 with a note each, same as today — Alpha just keeps it on the record.
